Left, every outside node is one hop from C or F, so the score is 5 / 5 = 1.0. Right, from A, B the distances are 1, 1, 2, 3 and 4, so the score is 5 / 11 = 0.455." width="100%"} Group closeness (Everett & Borgatti, 1999) measures how near the rest of the network is to a set of nodes: each node outside the group is as far away as its *nearest* member, and the score is the number of outside nodes divided by the sum of those distances. A high value means that, between them, the members can reach everyone quickly, which is the criterion for placing several facilities, seeding a campaign from a few starting points, or choosing a committee that is well connected to everyone. On directed graphs the distance is measured *to* the group (how quickly others can reach it), as in NetworkX. Nodes that cannot reach the group add nothing. Distances follow `shortest_path()`: hops, or total weight on a weighted graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [group]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The group's nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to measure distance by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The group closeness (`0` if no outside node can reach the group). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the group is empty, contains a node that does not exist, or weights are used and one is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a path of seven nodes, two members spread out along it are closer to everyone than two members side by side: ::: {#c4e013e6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(7) spread = path.group_closeness_centrality([2, 6]) bunched = path.group_closeness_centrality([3, 4]) round(spread, 3), round(bunched, 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.833, 0.556) ``` ::: :::
